use_case: UC2 – Ice-cream sales: do hot days and public holidays raise our sales? (Valdena Gelato Shop, IT)
objective_summary: Decide whether hot days (daily max temperature) and Italian public holidays measurably raise daily ice-cream sales at the shop, so that weekly orders can be planned around them. The plan first confirms that daily sales history exists for 2023-06-01 to 2025-05-31 (and recent window to 2026-03-31), that product codes can be mapped across the 2024 code change, and that weather and holiday covariates can be joined on date for a justified shop location.

need_plans.interpretation: Internal daily sales per product (ice-cream SKU/product code) at the shop, covering history (2023-06-01 to 2025-05-31) and recent (2025-06-01 to 2026-03-31) windows, at daily grain or finer, with a date key and quantity/revenue per product.
internal_queries: daily sales ice cream by product
acceptance_criteria: Daily grain or finer for every day in history and recent windows, or gaps are explicitly listed
Both windows covered without silent truncation; row counts per month reported
Quantity and/or revenue field with currency and unit stated
Data owner and refresh cadence recorded (unknown if not stated)
likely_pitfalls: Product codes changed in 2024; the same product may appear under two codes
Days with zero sales may be absent rather than zero
Opening-day gaps mistaken for zero demand
Timezone or till-day cut-off shifting sales across dates
Refund/void lines inflating or deflating quantities

need_plans.interpretation: A static mapping table (old code to new code, with validity dates and product description) that links product codes before and after the 2024 code change, so products can be compared across the break.
acceptance_criteria: Every product sold in the history window maps to exactly one current code, or is flagged as unmapped
Mapping date/effective period stated for the 2024 change
Mapping covers both directions and is versioned or dated
Products that cannot be mapped are listed so the forecast can exclude them
likely_pitfalls: One-to-many mappings (product split or merged) silently double-counting
Renamed products with same code treated as the same product
Mapping maintained only in a wiki or spreadsheet with no date
Codes reused for different products after the change

need_plans.interpretation: Daily maximum temperature (degrees C) for a justified shop location in northern Italy, covering both windows at daily grain, keyed by calendar date.
external_data_hints: Use the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (archive, reanalysis) for the chosen coordinates; daily temperature_2m_max, timezone stated, window 2023-06-01 to 2026-03-31. Record the chosen city as an assumption in decisions.md. Trap: reanalysis is modelled, not station observations; confirm the timezone used for the day boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Daily max temperature present for every date in both windows
Coordinates and timezone recorded and justified as an assumption
Terms: open-data licence accepted for prototyping and production per register
likely_pitfalls: Reanalysis is modelled, not station-measured; disclose
Timezone mismatch (UTC vs Europe/Rome) shifting the daily maximum
Probe calls should use short ranges only
Shop city not named in any source; location choice is an assumption

need_plans.interpretation: Daily flag for Italian national public holidays (and regional ones if relevant) for every date in both windows, keyed by calendar date, with holiday name.
external_data_hints: Nager.Date public holidays API, country IT, years 2023 through 2026; check for regional holidays (e.g. local patron saints) which Nager may not carry and which may need a separate Italian source.
acceptance_criteria: Every year covering both windows (2023-2026) returns a holiday list for IT
National holidays match the official Italian list; regional/local holidays flagged as missing if absent
Date key is calendar date; no timezone shift
likely_pitfalls: Regional or patron-saint holidays absent from national API
Holidays on weekends or shop closure days being confused with demand effects
Ferragosto and Easter Monday handling
Using a year outside the window

need_plans.interpretation: Daily shop opening/closing days (including closures and holidays when shut) and dated local events that could affect footfall, at daily grain across both windows.
external_data_hints: Local event calendar from the municipality or regional tourism portal for the shop's chosen town, daily grain, 2023-2026. Trap: event lists are often incomplete or undated; record coverage gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Opening/closure status available per day in both windows, or gaps listed
Event source named with publisher, dates and geography
Events have start and end dates at daily grain
likely_pitfalls: Closed days recorded as zero sales
Opening hours changed over time without a dated record
Event lists incomplete or back-dated

open_questions: Which Italian town is the shop in? Needed to choose Open-Meteo coordinates (no source names the city); the choice must be recorded as an assumption in decisions.md.
Do the internal POS exports include a per-product key that is stable across the 2024 code change, or is a manual mapping required?
Are there regional or local Italian holidays that apply to the shop's town and must be added beyond the national list?
Is there a dated record of shop closures and opening-hour changes for 2023-2026?
Does the owner accept modelled reanalysis temperature instead of station observations for the weather covariate?
Gap between windows: history ends 2025-05-31 and recent starts 2025-06-01; confirm there is no missing data at the boundary and that the recent window ends 2026-03-31 as specified.
